tactics.description: AbbVie built a wall of over 100 patents around Humira, including patents on manufacturing processes, formulations, and treatment methods, creating a 'patent thicket' that deterred biosimilar competition.
tactics.outcome: Multiple biosimilar entrants delayed by years through litigation risk

tactics.description: AbbVie reached settlements with multiple biosimilar manufacturers, granting them licenses to launch only after specific dates far beyond the original patent expiry.
tactics.ftc_case_ref: FTC v. AbbVie Inc. — Investigated anti-competitive patent settlement agreements
tactics.outcome: Biosimilar launches delayed until January 2023, years after original biologic patent expiry

tactics.description: Filed additional patents for citrate-free formulation and auto-injector device years after original approval to extend exclusivity period.
tactics.outcome: Extended effective exclusivity beyond original patent cliff

tactics.description: Celgene used its mandatory REMS safety program to restrict access to drug samples, preventing generic makers from conducting required bioequivalence testing.
tactics.ftc_case_ref: FTC complaint against Celgene Corp. (2024) — REMS abuse to block generic entry
tactics.outcome: FTC action filed; generic entry delayed by approximately 5 years

tactics.description: Celgene obtained multiple secondary patents on dosing regimens and treatment methods for Revlimid, extending beyond the original compound patent.
tactics.outcome: Generic competitors forced to design around patents or wait

tactics.description: Celgene settled with generic makers, allowing limited volumes initially then full entry years later.
tactics.court_case: In re Celgene Corp. Antitrust Litigation
tactics.outcome: Controlled generic entry with volume caps

tactics.description: Multiple method-of-use and formulation patents filed after initial approval to extend exclusivity.
tactics.outcome: Generic entry contested through 2028

tactics.description: Filed citizen petitions at FDA raising safety and bioequivalence concerns about potential generic versions.
tactics.outcome: Delayed FDA review of generic applications

tactics.description: J&J accumulated over 40 patents on Stelara covering manufacturing, formulation, and methods of treatment, creating barriers to biosimilar entry.
tactics.outcome: Multiple biosimilar applicants facing patent litigation

tactics.description: Filed patent infringement suits triggering 30-month stays of FDA approval for biosimilar applicants.
tactics.outcome: Automatic regulatory delay for each biosimilar applicant

tactics.description: Amgen obtained a secondary patent on the manufacturing process for Enbrel that extended protection to 2029, far beyond the original compound patent.
tactics.outcome: Biosimilar Erelzi (Sandoz) approved 2016 but blocked from launching

tactics.description: Rather than face true biosimilar competition, Amgen launched its own authorized biosimilar to control the competitive landscape.
tactics.outcome: Market entry of independent biosimilars further delayed

tactics.description: Filed additional patents covering combination therapies and new indications after initial approval to extend the exclusivity window.
tactics.outcome: Generic entry pushed beyond 2032

tactics.description: Multiple formulation and dosage patents filed to create barriers for generic entry.
tactics.outcome: Potential generics face complex patent landscape

tactics.description: Merck has filed extensive patents covering Keytruda's manufacturing, formulations, and numerous method-of-use applications across cancer types.
tactics.outcome: Biosimilar entry unlikely before 2030s despite biologic patent lifecycle

tactics.description: Continued filing new indication patents as Keytruda gains approvals in additional cancer types, extending the patent portfolio.
tactics.outcome: Each new indication adds potential patent protection

tactics.description: Novartis filed a patent on the beta crystalline form of imatinib mesylate to extend protection beyond the original compound patent. This was challenged internationally in landmark Supreme Court cases.
tactics.outcome: India's Supreme Court rejected the crystalline form patent in 2013; US generic entry eventually occurred in 2016

tactics.description: Filed over 40 secondary patents covering dosage forms, treatment methods for various cancers, and salt forms of imatinib.
tactics.outcome: Created litigation risk for generic manufacturers despite straightforward chemistry

tactics.description: Novartis launched its own authorized generic to capture generic market share and limit independent generic competition profitability.
tactics.outcome: Reduced incentive for additional generic entrants by capturing first-mover advantage in generic market

tactics.description: Gilead set the launch price at $84,000 for a 12-week course ($1,000/pill) despite production costs under $200. A Senate Finance Committee investigation found Gilead's pricing was designed to maximize revenue with no regard to patient access.
tactics.ftc_case_ref: US Senate Finance Committee Investigation, 2015 — 'The Price of Sovaldi and its Impact on the US Healthcare System'
tactics.outcome: Medicaid and prison systems rationed access; many patients denied treatment due to cost

tactics.description: Gilead built a portfolio of 52+ patents around sofosbuvir covering compound, formulation, combination therapy, and method-of-treatment claims.
tactics.outcome: Generic competition delayed until 2029+ in the US despite massive international generic production

tactics.description: Gilead reached settlements with generic manufacturers limiting early entry and establishing volume caps for authorized generics.
tactics.outcome: Controlled generic entry through licensing agreements

tactics.description: Biogen developed Vumerity (diroximel fumarate), a prodrug that converts to the same active metabolite as Tecfidera, to transition patients before generic entry.
tactics.outcome: Captured revenue by switching patients to patent-protected successor product

tactics.description: Biogen filed citizen petitions at FDA raising safety concerns about generic dimethyl fumarate bioequivalence.
tactics.outcome: Delayed FDA review of generic applications

tactics.description: Vertex has built an 82-patent fortress around Trikafta and its component molecules, creating one of the most extensive patent thickets for any drug.
tactics.outcome: No generic or biosimilar competition possible until late 2030s

tactics.description: As the sole manufacturer of effective CFTR modulators for cystic fibrosis, Vertex faces zero therapeutic competition, enabling sustained premium pricing with no market alternatives.
tactics.outcome: CF patients and insurers have no negotiating leverage; pricing power absolute

tactics.description: Regeneron and Sanofi have filed 64+ patents covering the dupilumab antibody, its various indications, dosing regimens, and manufacturing methods.
tactics.outcome: Biosimilar entry unlikely before early 2030s

tactics.description: Each new indication approval (eczema, asthma, COPD, prurigo nodularis, chronic sinusitis) adds method-of-treatment patents extending exclusivity beyond the original biologic patent.
tactics.outcome: Patent portfolio continuously expanding with each FDA approval

tactics.description: Like Revlimid, Celgene used the mandatory REMS safety program for thalidomide analogues to restrict sample access, preventing generic manufacturers from obtaining product for bioequivalence testing.
tactics.ftc_case_ref: FTC complaint against Celgene Corp. — REMS abuse pattern across IMiD portfolio
tactics.outcome: Generic entry delayed years beyond patent expiry

tactics.description: Built secondary patent portfolio on crystalline forms and treatment methods extending well beyond original compound patent.
tactics.outcome: Generic competitors face multi-year patent litigation delays

tactics.description: Gilead priced Harvoni at $94,500 for a 12-week course despite production costs under $250. Like Sovaldi, the pricing strategy prioritized maximum revenue over broad patient access.
tactics.outcome: State Medicaid programs rationed treatment; many patients with Hep C denied access due to cost

tactics.description: Gilead filed 58+ patents covering both component molecules and the combination, creating overlapping patent protection with the Sovaldi portfolio.
tactics.outcome: Generic competition delayed until 2030+ despite straightforward small-molecule chemistry

tactics.description: BMS obtained secondary patents on the monohydrate crystalline form of dasatinib, extending exclusivity 4 years beyond the original compound patent.
tactics.outcome: Generic entry delayed until late 2024 despite original patent expiring in 2020

tactics.description: Filed citizen petitions raising bioequivalence concerns about generic dasatinib formulations.
tactics.outcome: Delayed FDA review of generic applications

tactics.description: AbbVie has filed 47+ patents around venetoclax covering compound forms, combination therapies, and treatment methods, applying the same patent thicket strategy perfected with Humira.
tactics.outcome: Generic entry unlikely before mid-2030s

tactics.description: Continued filing combination therapy patents (venetoclax + obinutuzumab, venetoclax + azacitidine) extending protection well beyond the original compound patent.
tactics.outcome: Each combination approval adds method-of-treatment patent protection

tactics.description: Pfizer developed Xeljanz XR (extended-release) formulation to extend patent protection beyond the original compound patent, encouraging patients to switch to the patent-protected formulation.
tactics.outcome: XR formulation patents extend to 2028, well beyond original 2025 compound patent

tactics.description: Filed 42+ patents covering salt forms, formulations, and method-of-treatment patents for each approved indication.
tactics.outcome: Complex patent landscape creating barriers for generic entry

tactics.description: Regeneron launched Eylea HD (8mg, higher dose) in 2023 just as biosimilar competition for standard Eylea (2mg) emerged, attempting to shift patients to a new formulation with fresh patent protection.
tactics.outcome: Patients being transitioned to Eylea HD ahead of biosimilar launches for standard Eylea

tactics.description: Regeneron filed citizen petitions with FDA raising safety concerns about aflibercept biosimilars, delaying review timelines.
tactics.outcome: Some biosimilar approvals delayed by 6-12 months

tactics.description: Enzalutamide was developed with NIH funding at UCLA. Despite taxpayer-funded research, the drug was licensed exclusively to Medivation/Astellas and priced at over $150,000/year. UCLA attempted to use march-in rights but was denied.
tactics.outcome: Government declined to exercise march-in rights despite public funding origins

tactics.description: Multiple secondary patents filed on formulation and method-of-treatment after initial compound patent.
tactics.outcome: Generic entry delayed beyond original compound patent expiry

tactics.description: Lisdexamfetamine is a prodrug of dextroamphetamine. Shire created a patentable prodrug form of a molecule (amphetamine) that has been off-patent since the 1970s, enabling new patent protection and premium pricing for essentially the same active drug.
tactics.outcome: Generic amphetamine salts cost under $30/month; Vyvanse sold at $400/month until 2023

tactics.description: Shire/Takeda negotiated settlement with generic manufacturers to delay entry until August 2023.
tactics.outcome: Generic lisdexamfetamine entry delayed from 2021 to August 2023

tactics.description: Novartis filed 44 patents covering the antibody, formulations, autoinjector devices, and multiple treatment methods to build a broad exclusivity wall.
tactics.outcome: Biosimilar development timelines extended due to patent uncertainty

tactics.description: Continuous filing of method-of-treatment patents for each new indication approval extends the overall patent estate.
tactics.outcome: Each new indication adds years of protection via method patents

tactics.description: Gilead combines multiple APIs (bictegravir + emtricitabine + TAF) into single-tablet regimens, then patents the specific combination. Individual components may lose protection earlier, but the combination patent extends exclusivity.
tactics.outcome: Generic versions of individual components available internationally at under $50/month; US brand price remains $3,700/month

tactics.description: Filed 56 patents covering the combination, crystal forms, and treatment methods.
tactics.outcome: Broad patent estate discouraging generic challenges

tactics.description: Merck reached patent settlements with multiple generic manufacturers including Teva, Mylan, and Sun Pharma, granting them licenses to launch sitagliptin generics only after agreed-upon future dates well beyond original compound patent expiry.
tactics.outcome: Generic entry delayed until 2026 despite original compound patent expiring in 2022

tactics.description: Filed secondary patents on crystalline forms of sitagliptin phosphate and fixed-dose metformin combinations (Janumet) to extend effective exclusivity beyond the original compound patent.
tactics.outcome: Extended effective exclusivity from 2022 to 2026 through crystal form and combination patents

tactics.description: Filed citizen petitions with the FDA raising bioequivalence concerns for proposed generic sitagliptin products, triggering mandatory FDA review periods.
tactics.outcome: FDA review period added months of delay to generic approval timelines

tactics.description: Transitioned from 4-valent Gardasil to 9-valent Gardasil 9 with new patent protection, effectively resetting the patent clock on the HPV vaccine franchise while discontinuing the original product.
tactics.outcome: New composition patents extend protection to 2028+; no generic 4-valent Gardasil was ever launched

tactics.description: The 9-antigen virus-like particle vaccine requires highly specialized yeast fermentation and purification processes that create significant barriers to biosimilar development beyond patent protection.
tactics.outcome: No biosimilar HPV vaccine approved anywhere in the world as of 2024; manufacturing serves as de facto exclusivity

tactics.description: J&J used exclusionary contracts with hospitals and insurers, offering steep rebates contingent on excluding biosimilar infliximab products like Inflectra and Renflexis from formularies.
tactics.outcome: Despite biosimilar availability since 2016, Remicade maintained >80% market share for years through contracting

tactics.description: Offered bundled rebates across J&J's immunology portfolio, tying Remicade discounts to purchases of other J&J products to make biosimilar switching economically unfavorable.
tactics.ftc_case_ref: Pfizer Inc. v. Johnson & Johnson — antitrust suit over exclusionary Remicade contracts (filed 2017)
tactics.outcome: Pfizer (Inflectra) sued J&J for anticompetitive behavior; case settled 2021

tactics.description: Built a 95-patent estate around Botox covering formulations, manufacturing processes, treatment methods, and injection techniques, creating significant barriers to biosimilar development.
tactics.outcome: No FDA-approved Botox biosimilar as of 2024 despite original patent expiring in 2014

tactics.description: Botulinum toxin manufacturing requires specialized BSL-2 facilities and expertise in Clostridium fermentation; regulatory requirements for potency testing create additional barriers beyond patents.
tactics.outcome: Only two competitors (Dysport, Xeomin) have navigated the regulatory/manufacturing barriers; no interchangeable biosimilar

tactics.description: Continuously expanded approved indications (chronic migraine 2010, overactive bladder 2013, upper/lower limb spasticity) creating new method-of-use patents for each indication.
tactics.outcome: Each new indication brings new patents extending effective exclusivity for therapeutic uses

tactics.description: Developed and promoted subcutaneous formulation Rituxan Hycela (rituximab/hyaluronidase) with new patent protection, encouraging providers to switch from IV Rituxan before biosimilar entry.
tactics.outcome: Rituxan Hycela captured significant market share from IV Rituxan, partially shielding revenue from biosimilar competition

tactics.description: Filed secondary patents on specific treatment methods, particularly for rheumatoid arthritis, extending method-of-use exclusivity beyond the original antibody patent.
tactics.outcome: RA indication protected by method patents extending to 2026 despite original patent expiring in 2015
